outcome: Risk of obstetric anal sphincter injury (third- or fourth-degree tear)
cohort: 455,000 births in Victoria, Australia between 2009 and 2014
finding: This retrospective cohort study found that women having their first VBAC have a 21% increased risk of sustaining a third- or fourth-degree tear during childbirth compared to women having their first vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Women having their first VBAC have a significantly increased risk of sustaining a third- or fourth-degree tear, compared with primiparous women having a vaginal birth.
